actions.title: Read the decision boundary before choosing
actions.instruction: Read the scenario boundary: the Workshop Queue can keep stable human-readable text or adopt structured JSON. Both are valid choices for this exercise. Academy will verify that the ADR and decision-log entry agree with one accepted choice; it will not choose for you.
actions.rationale: A decision record is useful only when its alternatives and consequences are understood before an option is selected.
actions.expected_result: You can name both choices and the trade-off each one introduces.
actions.recovery: If the choice is still unclear, pause at this boundary and reread the scenario rather than drafting an ADR from a guessed conclusion.
actions.evidence: Your choice is a human decision. The final Check can inspect the recorded result, not the reasoning that led to it.

actions.title: Keep the prepared identity private
actions.instruction: Academy reads only a display-safe Git author name while preparing this attempt. Do not paste an email address, rejected name, or identity output into chat, an issue, or the ADR. The recorded ADR must use the prepared name, not a replacement invented later.
actions.rationale: The exercise proves attribution from committed evidence while keeping unnecessary personal data out of training artifacts.
actions.expected_result: You understand that author identity is prepared locally and that email is neither required nor retained.
actions.recovery: If Academy rejects the configured display name, correct it locally and start a preserved retry; never publish the rejected value as diagnostic evidence.
actions.evidence: Check derives the accepted name from Git commit metadata, not from a learner-supplied transcript.

actions.title: Keep Prepare behind the publication gate
actions.instruction: Do not run P03 Prepare from the current public Preview 0.6. P03 is not published or runnable there. This private card specifies a future published release contract: only an installed release whose manifest includes P03 in runnable_labs and guided_labs may expose Prepare through the Academy console.
actions.rationale: A private lesson may define reviewed future behavior, but it cannot invent an executable path or claim an unpublished operation succeeds.
actions.expected_result: No P03 Prepare runs in Preview 0.6, and the learner repository remains unchanged.
actions.recovery: If any private draft names an install path or tells a learner to run P03 Prepare, stop authoring and restore this publication gate; do not substitute source-checkout execution.
actions.evidence: academy/publication/preview-0.6.json lists P03 under coming_next and excludes it from runnable_labs and guided_labs.

actions.title: Inspect the existing decision context
actions.instruction: Use a native terminal to inspect the occupied ADR-0003 boundary and the append-only decision log. These are direct terminal commands, never harness passthrough commands, so they never begin with !.
actions.rationale: Reading the current record prevents overwriting ADR-0003 and exposes the exact append boundary for ADR-0004.

actions.recovery: If either source is missing or has unexpected local edits, stop and use Reset for a new baseline instead of recreating governance history by hand.
actions.evidence: The committed attempt must retain the prepared decision-log bytes as an append-only prefix.

actions.title: Ask for analysis without delegating the choice
actions.instruction: In your selected CodeArbiter harness, send this agent request. It is plain harness text, not a terminal command, so it never begins with !. The agent may analyze both alternatives; you choose the accepted option yourself.
actions.rationale: Analysis can make trade-offs legible without converting a learner-owned architecture decision into an agent-selected answer.

actions.recovery: If the agent chooses, writes, stages, or commits before you decide, stop. Preserve the attempt and reset rather than representing that action as your acceptance.

actions.title: Choose the summary format yourself
actions.instruction: After reading the comparison, copy exactly one choice into your selected CodeArbiter harness. This is your architecture direction, not an agent recommendation. Do not send both choices and do not ask the agent to decide between them.
actions.rationale: CodeArbiter may analyze alternatives and later draft the record, but only the learner may select the decision that the ADR attributes to them.

actions.recovery: If the agent selects a different option or begins drafting before one exact choice is sent, stop the lane and restate your choice; do not accept agent-owned direction as learner evidence.
actions.evidence: The copied statement is explicit learner-owned direction. Final Check can compare the recorded sentence, but it cannot prove who sent it.

actions.title: Have CodeArbiter draft the proposed ADR
actions.instruction: After sending one exact choice, invoke the host-native ADR lane in the selected harness. The command starts sanctioned proposed authoring; it does not accept the ADR, commit it, or guarantee P03's exact local Check shape by itself.
actions.rationale: The actual CodeArbiter lifecycle writes a user-attributed proposed ADR first and requires explicit learner instruction for any later transition to accepted.

actions.title: Inspect the exact proposed ADR and log contract
actions.instruction: Before acceptance or commit, inspect .codearbiter/decisions/0004-academy-lab.md and .codearbiter/decisions/decision-log.md. The ADR must still say status: proposed and include date:, title: Choose the Workshop Queue summary-format boundary, decided-by:, supersedes: none, and governs: workshop_queue/cli.py. Its H1 must be # ADR-0004 — Choose the Workshop Queue summary-format boundary; ordered headings must be Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences, Risks.
actions.rationale: P03 Check reads one exact artifact shape; a generic ADR filename, missing governs field, accepted-by-default draft, or plausible substitute cannot satisfy that contract.

actions.evidence: This inspection checks the exact files and proposed content that must later transition to accepted before the final P03 semantic Check can pass.

actions.title: Accept the reviewed proposal explicitly
actions.instruction: Only after the proposed ADR and appended log entry match your decision, copy this direction into your selected harness. Acceptance is a separate learner-owned status transition. It is not implied by ca-adr, silence, review, or the later commit command.
actions.rationale: CodeArbiter never advances proposed to accepted on its own judgment; an explicit learner instruction must precede the status change and commit.

The exact learner choice and all other reviewed content remain unchanged; nothing is committed.
actions.recovery: If anything besides the reviewed lifecycle fields changes, withdraw acceptance and inspect the diff. Do not run the commit gate until the accepted artifacts still match the proposal you approved.
actions.evidence: The copied sentence is explicit learner direction for acceptance; Check can verify final accepted state but cannot authenticate the conversation.

actions.title: Commit only after accepting both recorded boundaries
actions.instruction: Read the complete ADR and appended decision-log entry yourself. Only after you accept both the ADR content and the append boundary, ask the agent to run the host-native commit gate. This is a CodeArbiter command, never a ! terminal passthrough command.
actions.rationale: The learner acceptance boundary stays before the repository commit, so a committed record is never presented as proof of an unmade decision.

actions.title: Keep Check behind the publication gate
actions.instruction: Do not run P03 Check from the current public Preview 0.6; P03 is not published there. This private card specifies a future published release contract: after that release prepares P03 and the learner commits accepted evidence, its installed Academy console will own Check.
actions.rationale: The checked-in semantic predicate is maintainer test evidence, not permission to claim an unavailable public command ran or passed.
actions.expected_result: No P03 Check runs or records progress in Preview 0.6; only focused maintainer semantic tests evaluate the private contract.
actions.recovery: If private copy claims Check passed, remove that claim. Wait for a future published release that lists P03 as runnable, then rely only on that installed release's actual result.
actions.evidence: academy/publication/preview-0.6.json lists P03 as coming_next, while tests exercise the exact future Check predicate without presenting it as learner execution.

actions.title: Keep Reset behind the publication gate
actions.instruction: Do not run P03 Reset from the current public Preview 0.6 because P03 is not published there. This private card specifies a future published release contract: its Academy console may preserve a prepared P03 attempt and create a numbered retry only after that release exposes P03.
actions.rationale: Future recovery behavior can be reviewed privately without inventing an executable command or encouraging destructive manual cleanup.
actions.expected_result: No P03 Reset runs in Preview 0.6, so no learner branch or attempt is changed by this private lesson.
actions.recovery: Do not imitate future Reset with force-reset, branch deletion, or a source-checkout command. Preserve local authoring evidence and wait for the published operation contract.
actions.evidence: The current Preview 0.6 manifest is the release boundary; a future published release must provide and verify preservation semantics before this card becomes executable.
